newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-GRAF OUT, TOP WOMEN COLLAPSE IN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF OUT, TOP WOMEN COLLAPSE IN OPEN.

text.p: German tennis queen Steffi Graf was sensationally bundled out of the Australian Open on Sunday, joining a sudden exodus of top female seeds from the first Grand Slam event of the year.
Graf's campaign for a fifth Australian Open title was brought to an abrupt end by in-form South African Amanda Coetzer, who beat her 6-2 7-5 on a searing centre court.
It was the world number one's worst performance in Melbourne since she lost in the third round as a 14-year-old in 1984.

The top seed was the biggest casualty on a day of upsets and she follows fifth-seeded compatriot Anke Huber, Spain's third seed Conchita Martinez and American seventh seed Lindsay Davenport out of the tournament.

The day's big winner was 16-year-old Swiss Martina Hingis who did not have to play a shot on Sunday, sitting comfortably on the other side of the draw. The number four seed is now hot favourite to become the youngest Grand Slam champion in the history of professional tennis.
Coetzer, the number 12 seed, broke Graf on her first two service games and held on for a 6-2 win in the first set.
Graf, who has made hesitant starts all week, fought back to build up a 4-0 lead in the second set.
But with courtside temperatures of more than 40 degrees Celsius (104 Fahrenheit), she wilted in the heat and appeared to feel the effects of a lingering back injury.
Third seed Conchita Martinez appeared to be heading for an easy win against 16th seed Sabine Appelmans of Belgium after winning the first set 6-2 and serving for the match at 5-4 in the second.
Then she collapsed, going down 2-6 7-5 6-1 in the most remarkable turnaround in the tournament.

Number five seed Huber, who lost in the final last year to American Monica Seles, saw history repeat itself. The German was completely outclassed in losing 6-2 6-3 to former champion Mary Pierce, who also beat her in the fourth round on her way to the title in 1995.
American seventh seed Lindsay Davenport was beaten by unseeded compatriot Kimberly Po 7-6 6-4 in a tight match marked by a 15-13 first-set tie-break.

Sunday's drama means there are no top seeds left in the top half of the women's draw. Hingis already faced an easier time in the bottom half where her greatest threat will come from either number eight seed Irina Spirlea of Romania or 15th seed Chanda Rubin of the United States.

But Graf's defeat may allow her to return to Germany where her father Peter is on trial on charges of evading taxes on her earnings. The prosecution has asked for a jail sentence of six years and nine months and the verdict is expected on January 24 a few hours before the women's final.
In the men's draw, Michael Chang dropped the first set to Ukrainian hitman Andrei Medvedev then closed him out of the game to win 4-6 6-2 6-2 6-1.
It started off as a golden day for Spain and especially the former Olympic city of Barcelona. Barcelona baseliners Felix Mantilla and Carlos Moya both secured quarter-final berths.
Mantilla beat MaliVai Washington of the United States 7-5 6-2 6-1 and Moya won in five sets, 6-3 1-6 3-6 6-2 6-4, over Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman.
But the northeastern Spanish city saw its greatest tennis star, women's number three seed Martinez, dumped from the competition.
